response.sql: WITH matched_orders AS (SELECT DISTINCT o.recordvault, u.acctscope FROM riskandmargin rm INNER JOIN orders o ON rm.ordervault = o.recordvault INNER JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp), scope_counts AS (SELECT acctscope, COUNT(*) as scope_count FROM matched_orders GROUP BY acctscope), stats AS (SELECT SUM(scope_count) as total_count, CAST(SUM(scope_count) AS REAL) / COUNT(*) as avg_count FROM scope_counts) SELECT sc.acctscope as scope, sc.scope_count as count, CAST(sc.scope_count AS REAL) / s.total_count as share, CAST(sc.scope_count AS REAL) / s.avg_count as count_divided_by_avg FROM scope_counts sc CROSS JOIN stats s ORDER BY sc.acctscope;

assumptions.assumption: The request asks for the count of distinct orders (not risk/margin record pairs) that have at least one matching risk/margin record. Using DISTINCT ensures each order is counted once even if multiple risk/margin records reference it.

alternatives.interpretation: If the request intends to count all (order, risk/margin) pairs as separate items instead of deduplicating orders (e.g., to count the cardinality of the join result), remove DISTINCT from the matched_orders CTE.
